title: 7.4 · Show and credit
name: Show and credit
summary: Teams finish Credits, How-to and How it works in the question step (made by, idea from, art and sounds with the license of each, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines, how it works: the main rule and the variables), then demo circles of six: a sixty-second demo that names one choice and the user need behind it, then one question. The teacher visits each circle and marks the Explain & credit line.
iCan: write player instructions and a short How it works that names the main rule and the variables
credit the template, media and people the way each license asks
explain one design choice and the user need behind it
materials: Credits, How-to and How it works template printable (one per team)
demo card printable: who it is for, one choice and the need behind it, how to play, how it works (one per team)
the team folders with the captains' login cards
doNow: Who or what helped make your game? List everyone and everything, with what each one gave you. First names only.
plan: Arrive, captains log in, Do Now
Explore: a model demo and the template with How it works
Credits, How-to and How it works (8), then demo circles of six (10)

warmup.why: two retrieval items from the playtest, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from the playtest

do: Give the model demo yourself with the frog quiz, sixty seconds by the clock: who it is for, one choice and the user need behind it, how to play in three lines, how it works in one line: the score goes up by ten per right answer, three wrong answers end the game.

Put the template on the projector: Made by · Idea from · Art and sounds (with the license of each) · Thanks to our testers · How to play in three lines · How it works: the main rule and the variables. Fill How it works for the frog quiz with the class.
say: Documentation lets someone else follow, test and change your game.
"It works well" helps nobody. "The score goes up by ten per star, and zero lives ends the game" helps everyone.
Attribution is written the way each license asks: the template by its name, built-in art as built-in, a free sound with its license, an idea with the person's first name.
ask: Which How it works line would let a classmate change your game: it is fun, or three wrong answers end the game and the timer is twenty seconds?
explore.afterAsk: The second one. Write the two things every How it works needs on the board: the main rule, and each variable with what changes it.
explore.bigIdea: Document so a classmate could follow, test and change it; credit as each license asks.

play.protocol: credits, how-to and how it works in the question step, then demo circles
creditsTemplate: Made by: first names or avatars
Idea from: a teammate, a classmate, a game you like
Art and sounds: the built-in art, a free sound, anything a classmate made, each with its license
How to play, in three lines: what you do, how you win, how you lose
How it works: the main rule in one or two lines, and each variable with what changes it
demoCircles: Circles of six (two teams). Each team: sixty seconds of demo on its own device (who it is for, one choice and the user need behind it, how to play, how it works in one line), then sixty seconds for one question from the circle.
The listeners hold the demo card with the four things to listen for; the teacher visits each circle for one demo and marks the Explain & credit line on the lesson progress page afterwards.
lookFors: a How it works with no variable in it: ask what the score or the timer does
credits that thank but do not attribute: the license and the maker's name are missing
a demo that explains a feature instead of a choice: ask which user need the feature answers
play.misconception: Students think documentation is the How to play card alone; How it works is the part a classmate needs to change the game, and it has to name the rule and the variables.
earlyFinishers: write What version 2 would have on the back of the demo card, with the variable it would add
listen to a second circle and write one question for a team there

discuss: What would version 2 have, and which tester or teammate gave you that idea?
Whose How it works would let you change their game right now, and what would you change?
showMe: One team gives its sixty-second demo to the whole class on the projector and reads its How it works; the class names the rule and one variable it heard.

exit.sentencePrompt: Name one choice you are proud of and the user need behind it. Then write one How it works line, and the credit for one thing you reused, the way its license asks.
exit.frame: One choice I am proud of is ___ because our player ___. How it works: ___. Credit: ___ by ___ (license: ___).

Credits a reused thing with its maker and what its license asks for

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: the demo card with four boxes to point at: who, one choice, how to play, how it works
the template with the lines pre-printed and a license word bank: built-in, public domain, creative commons with credit, made by a classmate who said yes
a quiet team demos to the teacher alone, then to one other team
stretch: a How it works a classmate can follow to change one number in the game, then watch them do it
give the demo a second time to a different circle without the card, and take two questions

unpluggedTwin.title: Paper credits, How it works and demo circles
materials: each team's paper prototype or game
steps: Teams fill the template on paper: made by, idea from, art and sounds with the license of each, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines, how it works with the rule and the variables.
Circles of six: sixty seconds of demo with the paper prototype or the game, one choice and the need behind it, then one question.
Teams swap templates: can the other team say how to change one number in the game from the How it works alone?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: who or what helped make your game; list everyone and everything with what each one gave you, first names only.

Teams fill the paper template (made by, idea from, art and sounds with the license of each, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines, how it works with the rule and the variables), then demo circles of six: sixty seconds per team with the paper prototype or the game, one choice and the need behind it, then one question. No projector and no login needed; collect the templates for the teacher.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

add: every team demos to the whole class on the projector
the template swap: each team changes one number in another team's game from its How it works alone
the Unit 7 review on Brain Board, then version 2 planned on paper

notes: Mark the Explain & credit line (0 to 3) on the lesson progress page after the circles; Also mark these teammates gives the whole team the marks. The Plan, Roles / timeline, Program and Test with others lines were marked on the earlier lessons of this unit.
No full names anywhere in the Builder or the game: credits use first names or avatars, and the class Games tab shows the same.
The template follows the credit block from Share or keep: template, art, ideas, sounds and testers, each with its license.
A game whose scan was flagged is demoed from the maker's screen; everything else is visible to the class on the Games tab.
Captains sign in; the question step is the team's.
Vocabulary beyond the four on the learn card: license, instructions.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: Who or what helped make your game? List everyone and everything, with what each one gave you. First names only.

Big idea: Document so a classmate could follow, test and change it; credit as each license asks.

Today: finish your credits, How to play and How it works, then demo circles: sixty seconds, one choice and the need behind it, one question.

We will talk about:
- What would version 2 have?
- Whose How it works would let you change their game right now?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Credits, How-to and How it works

levels: Nothing yet: no demo and no credits
Attempted: a demo or credits, but no choice is explained
Meets: the demo names one choice and why, How to play is three lines, How it works names the main rule and the variables, credits list template, media and ideas as each license asks
Exceeds: the reason refers to the user's need, and the documentation would let a classmate change the game

steps.body:
Fill in every line. First names or avatars only, never full names.
- Made by: ___
- Idea from: ___ (a teammate, a classmate, a game you like)
- Art and sounds: ___ (the built-in art, a free sound, anything a classmate made), each with its license
- Thanks to our testers: ___
- How to play, in three lines: what you do, how you win, how you lose.
- How it works: the main rule in one or two lines, then each variable (score, lives, timer) and what changes it.
- Our demo: the one choice we will explain, and the user need behind it.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about documentation and credits.

steps.title: In your own words
steps.body:
Name one choice you are proud of and the user need behind it. Then write one How it works line, and the credit for one thing you reused, the way its license asks.
